findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses invalid computed zod keys, so every sync-mode refresh fails validation
findings.body: In zod, object shape keys must be string literals. `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate to the literal keys `"[object ZodString]"` and `"[object ZodOptional]"`, not dynamic key matchers. The resulting schema therefore requires the token response to contain a property literally named `[object ZodString]` with a number value, which no real token endpoint returns. Whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, every parseRefreshTokenResponse call fails with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', breaking token refresh for Google Calendar, Office 365 Calendar, Zoom, and Salesforce in exactly the mode this PR introduces. Use z.record() or .passthrough()/catchall() instead.

findings.title: Sync-mode refresh returns a fetch Response, but code reads res.data
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response when credential syncing is enabled (it only returns the googleapis `res` object in the non-sync branch). The code then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. A fetch Response has no `data` property, so `token` is undefined and reading `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. It is swallowed by the catch (message isn't 'invalid_grant'), so the Google access token is silently never refreshed when credential syncing is enabled, and calendar access breaks once the stored token expires.

findings.title: Sync-mode refresh result treated as HubspotToken but is a fetch Response
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint, but the code treats the result as a HubspotToken: it reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` (undefined, so expiryDate becomes NaN) and calls `hubspotClient.setAccessToken(hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken)` (undefined). The NaN expiry and undefined access token are then persisted to the credential row via prisma.credential.update, corrupting the stored HubSpot credentials. The Response body is never parsed.

findings.title: Sync-mode refresh response doesn't match expected Lark RefreshTokenResp shape
findings.body: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw Response from the self-hoster's endpoint, which per the PR description contains only an access token and expiry. The code then calls handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp) and reads `data.data.refresh_token`, `data.data.refresh_expires_in`, and `data.data.expires_in`. These fields don't exist on the sync response, so `data.data` is undefined and the refresh throws, making Lark calendar refresh always fail when credential syncing is enabled. The non-Lark response shape is never mapped onto LarkAuthCredentials.

findings.title: Sync-mode refresh response can't satisfy webexRefreshedTokenSchema (requires refresh_token)
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but the code still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires `refresh_token: z.string()` and `refresh_token_expires_in: z.number()`. The parse therefore always fails in sync mode and refreshAccessToken rejects with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', so Webex meetings stop working as soon as the access token expires. Unlike the other apps converted in this PR, Webex was not switched to parseRefreshTokenResponse.

findings.title: Sync-mode Zoom refresh computes expiry_date as NaN and overwrites refresh_token with placeholder
findings.body: In sync mode the endpoint returns only an access token and expiry (no `expires_in`, no `refresh_token`). parseRefreshTokenResponse fills in `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when absent, and this code then does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` (the literal string "refresh_token") and `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` where expires_in is undefined, producing NaN. Both the corrupted refresh token and NaN expiry are persisted to the credential row, permanently breaking future Zoom refreshes for that user until they reconnect.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as the Cal.com userId to the sync endpoint
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId: number | null` and is sent to the self-hoster's sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Here the code passes `credentialId` (the credential row's primary key) instead of `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint will therefore receive a wrong user id and either fail to find the user's tokens or return tokens for the wrong user. The sibling zohocrm service correctly passes `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Webhook updates only the first matching credential; duplicates keep stale keys
findings.body: The webhook looks up an existing credential with findFirst({ userId, appId }) and updates only that one row. Cal.com can legitimately have multiple credentials for the same user+app (e.g., office365video/webex/zoom callbacks historically created duplicates, and users can reconnect creating additional rows, plus there is no unique constraint on (userId, appId)). Any additional rows retain the old keys and may still be picked up by findFirst-based lookups elsewhere, so the 'source of truth' sync silently leaves stale credentials active. Consider updating all matching rows or enforcing one credential per (userId, appId).

findings.title: Secret comparison is not constant-time and handler lacks method/parse guards
findings.body: The webhook secret is compared with a plain `!==` on header values, which is a non-constant-time comparison for a bearer-style secret; use a timing-safe comparison. Also, the handler accepts any HTTP method (GET requests will run the full credential write path), and the zod `parse` on req.body plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` are unguarded, so malformed payloads produce unhandled 500s instead of 4xx responses.

findings.title: Sync-mode MS Teams refresh yields NaN expiry_date, causing refresh loop on every call
findings.body: In sync mode the endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, with no `expires_in`. The code computes `responseBody.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + (responseBody?.expires_in || 0) * 1000)`, i.e. approximately Date.now(), and persists that to the credential. Since isExpired compares expiry_date < Date.now(), the token is immediately considered expired again, so every API call triggers another sync-endpoint refresh round-trip; and if the sync response's own expiry field is never mapped, the stored expiry is effectively meaningless. Map the sync response's expiry onto expiry_date instead of relying on expires_in.
